Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 23-Nov-2024 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. (COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING) EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2024  
  SUBJECT: CSE 3121/CSE_3121 - PRINCIPLES OF CRYPTOGRAPHY  
  
  
  PRINCIPLES OF CRYPTOGRAPHY [CSE 3121]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                                  Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)                                                                                                                                         (5)  
  
  
1B)               Assess how a cryptographic hash function can be used to ensure message authentication. Use the scenario             (3)  
  where a sender computes a hash value of a message and transmits both the message and the hash to the  
  receiver.  
1C)               Apply Miller Rabin Algorithm to test the primality of the number 929, with base 2 (Show all the iterations of the   (2)  
  Algorithm including 0th)  
  
2A)               In a public-key system using RSA, you intercept the ciphertext C=31 sent to a user whose public key is e=7,         (5)  
  n=55. Evaluate the plaintext M.  
2B)               Generate the random bit stream (the first 5 bits) using Blum Blum Shub (BBS) Generator which uses the primes (3)  
  $$419 and 619, and a seed = 3456.$$  
2C)               Demonstrate on how the interchanging of 2 pairs of operations of Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)                 (2)  
  decryption algorithm to generate the equivalent Inverse Cipher in AES are justified.  
3A)               Explain the working of XTS-AES mode of operation of block cipher (assuming that the last Plaintext Block is         (4)  
  incomplete) on a sector of a device, for encryption and decryption with relevant block diagrams. Also, write the  
  equations for the same.  
3B)               Alice and Bob use the Diffie-Hellman key exchange method with a common prime q=17 and a primitive root a=3 (4)  
  $$i) If Alice chooses a private key XA =15 ,calculate her public key YA .$$  
  $$ii) If Bob chooses a private key XB =10 calculate his public key YB .$$  
  iii) Determine the shared secret key K that Alice and Bob will derive from their public keys. Write the formula for  
  the key calculation of Alice and Bob  
3C)               Differentiate between Pseudorandom Number Generators (PRNGs) and Pseudo Random Functions (PRFs) in                  (2)  
  
  terms of any 4 aspects.  
4A)               Analyse characteristics of True Random and Pseudorandom Number Generators with example.                             (4)  
4B)               Analyze the Playfair cipher's encryption process for the plaintext 'ENDTERM' using the keyword 'GRAVITY'.           (3)  
  Describe how the cipher handles repeated letters and spaces in the text and illustrate each encryption step.  
  Page 1 of 2

4C)   Illustrate with a neat diagram various ways through which a hash code can be used to provide message            (3)  
  authentication?  
5A)   In the context of communications across a network, explain various attacks can be identified. Discuss various   (4)  
  measures to deal with these attacks.  
5B)   Assess the strengths and limitations of the AES and DES algorithms in terms of security, efficiency, and        (3)  
  suitability for modern encryption needs. Evaluate which algorithm is more appropriate for contemporary  
  applications and justify your reasoning.  
5C)   In an RSA system, the public key of a given user is e = 65, n = 2881. What is the private key of this user?     (3)  
  
  
  -----End-----
